cases.title: Scalar loop control
cases.intent: Establish the scalar control for summing eight runtime-derived values without a source collection.
cases.oracle: Sum n+i for i=0..7: 8*n+28.
cases.focus: probe performs the same eight-value sum as cases 02–05 without constructing a list.

cases.title: Bounded list consumed locally
cases.intent: Positive control for existing intrafunction bounded-list promotion; inspect emitted allocation rather than assume it survives LLVM.
cases.oracle: Eight elements n through n+7 sum to 8*n+28.
cases.focus: probe constructs and reads one fixed-eight list entirely within the same function.

cases.title: Bounded list passed to a reader
cases.intent: Positive control for the strict borrowed-call promotion prototype, using a looped reader instead of a scalar leaf.
cases.oracle: sum_values reads n through n+7 without mutation: 8*n+28.
cases.focus: probe constructs the bounded list; sum_values is the ordinary list-parameter call boundary to inspect.

cases.title: Construction helper returns a list
cases.intent: Compare a constructor that returns its storage with the local and caller-created forms; measure the actual retained construction boundary.
cases.oracle: make_values creates n through n+7; their sum is 8*n+28.
cases.focus: make_values returns its constructed list to probe, which passes it to sum_values.

cases.title: Caller-created mutable destination
cases.intent: Exercise the proposed caller-initializes/helper-mutates pattern with the same values as the returned-list case; observe any inlining or allocation elimination.
cases.oracle: The empty destination receives n through n+7; its sum is 8*n+28.
cases.focus: probe creates the empty list before fill_values mutates it; sum_values reads the completed destination.

cases.title: Runtime-sized list
cases.intent: Control for a list whose capacity depends on runtime input rather than a small compile-time bound.
cases.oracle: n values n+i for i=0..n-1 sum to n*n+n*(n-1)/2.
cases.focus: probe uses n as the fill-loop bound, then lends the list to the same looped reader.

cases.title: Bounded list above the promotion limit
cases.intent: Control for a proven constant capacity whose 600 eight-byte integers exceed the current 4096-byte per-list promotion limit.
cases.focus: probe has a fixed 4800-byte element payload before the header; sum_values remains a borrowing reader.

cases.title: Read-only alias
cases.intent: Observe whether a read-only source alias adds ownership operations when neither name is consumed or mutated.
cases.oracle: Both names read the same eight-value sum, so the answer is 2*(8*n+28).
cases.focus: probe keeps values and snapshot live across two borrowed reads of the same logical contents.

cases.title: Snapshot retained across append
cases.intent: Require preservation of the old eight-element snapshot while a new version appends a ninth value; expose real copy-on-write and lifetime costs.
cases.oracle: Old sum is 8*n+28; new sum is 9*n+36. Weighted result is 10*(8*n+28)+(9*n+36)=89*n+316.
cases.focus: probe appends after taking snapshot, then reads both versions; the weighted output detects snapshot corruption.

cases.title: Snapshots retained across loop iterations
cases.intent: Exercise loop-carried sharing and managed children by retaining every list prefix until after construction.
cases.oracle: Prefix j contains j*n+j*(j-1)/2 for j=1..n. Summing prefixes gives n*(n+1)*(4*n-1)/6.
cases.focus: probe stores each version in history before the next append; the second loop reads all preserved versions through sum_values.

cases.title: Scalar record passed to a loop reader
cases.intent: Use a six-field scalar record as a control for aggregate argument handling without managed payloads.
cases.oracle: The six fields sum to 6n+15. The reader adds that sum and i for i=0..n-1, giving n(6n+15)+n(n-1)/2=(13n^2+29n)/2.
cases.focus: score (line 10) reads six scalar fields in a runtime-length loop; probe constructs and passes the record by value. Any scalar replacement is a valid optimization win.

cases.title: Returned record with a managed list field
cases.intent: Observe allocation and ownership when a factory returns a record containing a runtime-sized list and another function reads its field.
cases.oracle: make_batch stores the integers 1 through n and factor n. score computes n times their sum, n^2(n+1)/2.
cases.focus: make_batch (line 6) fills and returns Batch.items; score (line 13) borrows that field during a loop. The record and its list have different storage lifetimes.

cases.title: Record snapshot kept across managed-field mutation
cases.intent: Measure required snapshot preservation when a mut helper appends to a record's shared list while the original record remains observable.
cases.oracle: The saved record scores n+(n+n+1)=3n+1. The updated record has stamp 2n and appends 1..n, so it scores 4n+1+n(n+1)/2. Print 1000 times the saved score plus the updated score.
cases.focus: probe (line 19) keeps saved alive across extend (line 6), which mutates current.items and current.stamp; both records are read afterwards.

cases.title: Construct and traverse nested lists
cases.intent: Observe ownership transfer of fixed-width inner lists into a runtime-sized outer list, followed by nested borrowing in another function.
cases.oracle: Row i contains i, i+1 and i+2, whose sum is 3i+3. Summing rows i=0..n-1 gives 3n(n+1)/2.
cases.focus: make_rows (line 1) inserts each inner list into rows; score (line 11) traverses both levels. Inner lists have fixed length but escape into a managed container.

cases.title: List of records with dynamic text and list fields
cases.intent: Exercise managed-element insertion, field borrowing and destruction with dynamically produced strings and independently allocated integer lists.
cases.oracle: Entry i has label length 4+digits(n+i), two values, and value sum n+i. Its contribution is 6+digits(n+i)+n+i. For n=4 all labels use one digit, giving 50; for n=11 all use two digits, giving 264.
cases.focus: make_entries (line 6) constructs Entry(label="row:"+str(i+n), values=[i,n]); score (line 13) reads both managed fields. Labels are runtime text rather than only immortal literals.

cases.title: Branch-selected alias mutated beside both originals
cases.intent: Expose alias joins and copy-on-write when one of two lists is selected by a runtime branch, extended, and compared with both original values.
cases.oracle: The original sums are L=2n+1 and R=4n+1. Appending n+2 gives selected sum 3n+3 for even n or 5n+3 for odd n. Print 100L+10R+selected: 1085 and 2808.
cases.focus: choose (line 1) returns an input alias; probe (line 14) appends to the selected value and then reads both originals. The two input sizes exercise different branches.

cases.title: Runtime-selected callback reads a short list
cases.intent: Measure the ownership and allocation boundary of an indirect read-only call on a fixed-length scalar list; permit any valid devirtualization.
cases.oracle: The four values n..n+3 sum to 4n+6. Even n chooses sum_values; odd n chooses double_values, so the outputs are 22 and 2*50=100.
cases.focus: apply (line 15) invokes a function-valued parameter; probe (line 19) selects the callback from runtime parity and constructs the four-element list.

cases.title: Recursive reader of a short scalar list
cases.intent: Observe how an ordinary list borrow crosses recursive calls where the current strict proof remains conservative.
cases.oracle: sum_from visits each index from zero through three once and returns zero at index four. Its result is n+(n+1)+(n+2)+(n+3)=4n+6.
cases.focus: sum_from (line 1) forwards the same list through recursion; probe (line 7) creates a fixed-length list of runtime-dependent values.

cases.title: Returned managed field kept beside its parent
cases.intent: Expose ownership of a list returned from a borrowed record, then mutate the extracted value while retaining the parent snapshot.
cases.oracle: The parent's list sums to 3n+3. Appending n+3 to the extracted list produces sum 4n+6 while the parent remains unchanged. The final checksum is 100(3n+3)+(4n+6)+n=305n+306.
cases.focus: values_of (line 6) returns packet.values; probe (line 17) appends to that returned field and then reads packet.values and packet.id. Inlining the accessor is allowed.

cases.title: Loop-carried list rebuilt by a by-value helper
cases.intent: Measure copies and reference counts when each loop iteration replaces its list with the result of an ordinary by-value batch-append helper, without retaining snapshots.
cases.oracle: Let w=n%3+1. Iteration i appends n+i+j for j=0..w-1. The score adds the final length nw to the sum, giving nw(3n+w)/2. With (n,w)=(4,2) and (11,3), this is 56 and 594.
cases.focus: append_batch (line 1) makes a mutable local from an ordinary input and appends in a runtime-length loop; probe (line 15) carries the returned list into the next call.

cases.title: Unique scalar dictionary updates
cases.intent: Construct a dictionary and replace its values while it has one owner.
cases.oracle: Sum of i+1+n for i=0..n-1: n(n+1)/2+n^2.
cases.focus: probe lines 2-6 construct and update the same dictionary; lines 8-9 consume every value.

cases.title: Dictionary snapshot across updates
cases.intent: Keep an alias alive across the same scalar dictionary updates and consume both versions.
cases.focus: probe line 5 keeps the original dictionary live; line 7 mutates values; line 10 reads both versions.

cases.title: Managed text dictionary values
cases.intent: Insert runtime strings into a dictionary, replace each with a concatenated value, then read them.
cases.oracle: Each entry has length 7+decimal_digits(i+n); sum (i+1) times that length. For n=4 all values have one digit, and for n=11 all have two.
cases.focus: probe lines 4 and 6 allocate or replace managed text values inside an integer-keyed dictionary.

cases.title: Unique Unicode text append
cases.intent: Append a short Unicode piece repeatedly without publishing an alias.
cases.oracle: The text has 3n codepoints; the first lambda is at index 2 for n>0. Result: 51n+2.
cases.focus: probe lines 2-4 build Unicode text; line 5 consumes its length and search result.

cases.title: Text snapshot across append
cases.intent: Retain the pre-append text and consume both its original content and the extended version.
cases.oracle: Original length=3n, new length=4n, original z index=-1, new z index=3n. Result: 300n+4n-1+3n=307n-1.
cases.focus: probe line 5 preserves the original text across line 7 appends; line 8 observes both versions.

cases.title: Escaping Unicode substring
cases.intent: Return a three-codepoint substring from a helper, discard the source binding, and consume the substring.
cases.oracle: The slice always has three codepoints and starts at character n modulo 3 of a/lambda/z. Result: 300+ord(character), giving 1255 or 422.
cases.focus: segment line 2 returns the slice; probe lines 9-11 keep it after rebinding the source. Materialization versus sharing is to be measured.

cases.title: Unique byte-buffer append
cases.intent: Build a mutable buffer from runtime byte values and read its weighted checksum.
cases.oracle: Let b_i=(17i+n) mod256 for 0<=i<3n. Result: sum (i+1)b_i.
cases.focus: probe lines 2-4 construct and append to the buffer; lines 6-7 consume its bytes.

cases.title: Immutable bytes snapshot across append
cases.intent: Convert a buffer to immutable bytes, append to the buffer, and consume both versions.
cases.oracle: The snapshot has 3n bytes b_i=(17i+n) mod256. The buffer adds 255. Result: 30000n+2 sum b_i+255.
cases.focus: probe line 5 publishes immutable bytes; line 6 appends; lines 7-11 consume both. Copy versus shared storage is to be measured.

cases.title: Materialized filtered list
cases.intent: Materialize an input list and a filtered result with runtime sizes, preserving filtered order in a checksum.
cases.oracle: The selected n values are m,m+3,...,m+3(n-1), where m=3ceil(n/3). Weighted sum: n(n+1)(m+2n-2)/2.
cases.focus: probe lines 2-3 build the input and filtered lists; lines 5-6 read the materialized result.

cases.title: Large nonmonotone scalar sort
cases.intent: Sort 300+n runtime-derived integers, beyond the small-sort paths, and consume their order. Ordinary malloc scratch is a counter blindspot to check, not a measured byte claim.
cases.oracle: Independently numerically sort the multiset {(73i+19n) mod1009 | 0<=i<300+n}, then sum its kth element times k+1. Expected values computed with Python sorted.
cases.focus: probe line 3 sorts 304 or 311 nonmonotone integers. Source dispatch reaches core_sort.c scalar radix scratch malloc beyond 256 elements; managed counters exclude that malloc.
